answer: An agent marketplace requires a separate collateral bond for every identity allowed to trade opal, onyx, or crystal. Each bond stays locked for 30 days after that identity’s last trade, so an attacker cannot recycle the same funds across a swarm of disposable accounts. Creating 1,000 active identities therefore ties up 1,000 bonds, imposing a capital cost that grows with the swarm even when generating new keys is free.
